title: Sectionwise module pasting for direct-image composition and open restriction
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. On small representatives of the small pro-etale sites of schemes in a common universe [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] and $\mathcal M_T=\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T}$. Use the module direct images $a_*$, inverse images $a^*$ and their specified adjunctions [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback], and the exact open extension by zero $j_!\dashv j^*$ [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek]. Assume the canonical coefficient maps $\alpha_a:a^{-1}\Lambda_T\to\Lambda_S$ are isomorphisms for the morphisms under consideration; identify module inverse image with sheaf inverse image whose action is transported by $\alpha_a^{-1}$.
For $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$, write $c_{g,f}:(gf)_*\xrightarrow{\sim}g_*f_*$ for the inverse of the specified module composition isomorphism; its underlying map is restriction along the canonical fibre-product isomorphism [def-sfb-finite-lower-star-comp]. For $f:S\to T$ and an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow T$, put $S_U=S\times_TU$, with maps $j_S:S_U\hookrightarrow S$ and $f_U:S_U\to U$. Let $\beta_{f,j}:j^*f_*\xrightarrow{\sim}(f_U)_*j_S^*$ be the open-slice comparison of [lem-sfb-proetale-open-restriction-counit], initially over actual inverse-image rings and then transported by the coefficient isomorphisms. Then these are natural module isomorphisms with the following simultaneous normalization and coherence.

(a) For every module $M$ on $S$ and site object $V\to U$, $\beta_{f,j,M}(V)$ is the canonical identification $M(S\times_TV)\cong M(S_U\times_UV)$, hence the identity after the canonical identification of fibre products. The action is that obtained from $\alpha_j^{-1}$ and $\alpha_{j_S}^{-1}$. The transformations $c$ and $\beta$ are the lifts of these underlying sheaf maps, including their specified coefficient actions.

(b) For $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ\xrightarrow hT$, one has
$$ (h_*c_{g,f})\circ c_{h,gf}=(c_{h,g}f_*)\circ c_{hg,f}. $$

(c) For successive opens $W\xrightarrow vU\xrightarrow jT$, put $S_W=S\times_TW$ and let $v_S:S_W\hookrightarrow S_U$ be the pulled-back open. Under the canonical comparisons $(jv)^*\cong v^*j^*$ and $j_{S_W}^*\cong v_S^*j_S^*$, one has
$$\beta_{f,jv}=(\beta_{f_U,v}j_S^*)\circ(v^*\beta_{f,j}).$$
Here $j_{S_W}:S_W\hookrightarrow S$ is the composite open.

(d) For $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gT$ and $j:U\hookrightarrow T$, put $Y_U=Y\times_TU$, $X_U=X\times_TU$, with opens $j_Y,j_X$ and restricted maps $g_U,f_U$. Then
$$((g_U)_*\beta_{f,j_Y})\circ(\beta_{g,j}f_*)\circ(j^*c_{g,f})=(c_{g_U,f_U}j_X^*)\circ\beta_{gf,j}.$$
All equations include the canonical functor associators and fibre-product identifications. The identity-morphism and identity-open comparisons are identities under their canonical unit identifications. The equations are equalities of module morphisms, not just underlying abelian-sheaf maps, and hold degreewise for every cochain complex with their differentials [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. No derived-category assertion, properness or finite/discrete-coefficient hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Retain the specified internal module functors, coefficient maps and adjunctions. Forget the scalar-extension/comap-inverse comparison inverseImageActionIso to obtain underlyingPullbackIso. Its composite with the module adjunction unit is the ordinary sheaf adjunction unit: apply upperStarLowerStarAdjunction_homEquiv_hom and extendUnitHom_extendScalarsIsoComapInv_hom_app. Thus no arbitrary sectionwise action or coefficient identification is introduced.

For an open immersion, compose underlyingPullbackIso with the existing sheaf upperStarIsoLocalizationRestriction. Uniqueness of left adjoints identifies the units. The localization unit on sections is restriction along the counit of the object-composition/base-change adjunction. Naturality and its left triangle identity show that this localization isomorphism sends coprojection(j,M,E,s) to s. Since the localization comparison is invertible, every coprojection is bijective. The same argument applies to every pulled-back open, including identities and empty schemes.

For a square i f = fU j, form squarePushIso from the specified lowerStarComp, lowerStarCongr, and inverse lowerStarComp. Define betaMap as its inverse mate under i-star and j-star. The existing formulas for module compositors after forgetting give squarePushIso_section, and the unit equation for mates gives betaMap_on_unit. Naturality then computes betaMap on coprojections. The two arrows from the iterated pullback to the direct pullback agree on both projections, so the fibre-product universal property proves the exact sectionArrow formula in Sectionwise.

The sectionArrow is the Beck-Chevalley comparison pullbackMapComparison for the flipped cartesian square. The existing isIso_pullbackMapComparison_of_isPullback makes it invertible. Its section map and both coprojections are bijective, so betaMap has bijective components. The abelian-category, sheaf and module forgetful functors reflect isomorphisms. Hence asIso(betaMap) defines the comparison family beta and satisfies Sectionwise, with no choice of mere-existence data.

Composition is the inverse of the existing module lowerStarComp_assoc equality, and its underlying section formula follows from lowerStarComp_hom_app_hom and the sheaf inverse-compositor formula. Package the existing upperStar coherence, lowerStar adjunctions, and open lower-shriek adjunctions in a private CompactSupportFormalism. By conjugateIsoEquiv_upperStarComp, betaMap is exactly its pfBaseChange. The already-proved pfBaseChange_paste_horiz and pfBaseChange_paste_vert give SuccessiveOpens and MixedPasting, respectively. The conjugate pfComp is exactly the inverse specified lowerStarComp, so these equations have precisely the requested compositors and associators.

The formalism identity-square laws give the identity-open normalization. For the identity-morphism normalization, use sqIso_id_vert_hom and mateEquiv_id_id_unitors; the conjugate pfId is the specified lowerStarId. Existing lowerStarComp_id_left and lowerStarComp_id_right give the two composition unit laws. Finally apply naturality of beta.hom and lowerStarComp.inv to every differential K.d n m, giving Degreewise.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q10-9da732bf2 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: First delivery, with the statement unchanged from base. The item is still unsplit in live and side-live, is not in a dropped list and has no repair note. The delivery is one item commit plus its report, with no new nodes. The three added stmt_deps (module objects, fibre product, module upper-star comp) are notions the statement uses, and proof_deps is the union of the step uses. I checked the typing of (b), (c) and (d) through the identifications X×_Y Y_U≅X_U and S_U×_U W≅S_W, and tested identity f or j, identity factors, empty U or W and the empty scheme. Step 1: section-ring-lax-pushforward-coherence with ψ=η_a gives exactly Res_η mapMod(f_*), with the identity as underlying map. Step 3: the unit of Lan+sheafify at an object over U is the identity, because (W, graph) is initial in I_W, so η_j=α_j; the scalar-extension isomorphism is verbatim from def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations. Step 4: eta-comp applied to jf_U=fj_S gives b_A η_f=η_{f_U} a_V, and I re-derived that the two scalar actions match. Step 5: open-restriction-counit holds for arbitrary f and R; with M restricted along α_f its f_* action is η_f; linearity comes from step 4. Steps 6, 8 and 9 equate fibre-product maps by their projections. Step 7: α_{jv}=α_vα_j, and the conjugate characterization of def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp fixes the comparison. Steps 10–11 cover identities via eta-id and naturality at the differentials. The parent derived-open-coherence uses exactly c, β, (b)–(d) and the identity cases. Source: blueprint sk-thm-sf-comp-composition, 'Canonicity and associativity'; Stacks 09A5, 00XZ, 03D3 and 03DH match their labels; no SGA. I accept the 16 declared tool uses as generic sheaf and coefficient tools. I found no duplicate in the DAG. Advisory only: step 3 cites the continuous-functor adjunction rather than def-sfb-finite-upper-lower-star-adjunction, which is the same construction; stage 2 should pin β sectionwise. No fixes.
